subject: Overlapping session counts in Feb 1-3 usage — possible double-counting
messages:
From: Elena Vasquez <elena@starlite.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 7 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Overlapping session counts in Feb 1-3 usage — possible double-counting

Hi Karthik —

We're seeing an unexpected spike in billed usage for Feb 1-3 on account STL-9001 (Starlite AI). Our internal meter shows ~18% fewer aggregate tokens than the invoice. We tracked this down to what looks like overlapping session records where the same session_id appears multiple times across reconnects.

Attached is a small CSV (starlite_sessions.csv) with a few examples:
- session_923a, 2026-02-01T22:12:03Z, 14,321 tokens
- session_923a, 2026-02-01T22:12:08Z, 13,980 tokens
- session_9b7f, 2026-02-02T03:55:10Z, 2,100 tokens
- session_9b7f, 2026-02-02T03:55:11Z, 2,105 tokens

Can you explain whether Redwood's metering deduplicates rapid reconnects or overlapping websocket sessions? If not, it looks like some reconnects were billed as separate sessions. This is causing a material overage on our Feb invoice.

We'd appreciate a quick check and an export of the raw metering events for Feb 1-3 so we can reconcile. Happy to hop on a call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Elena Vasquez
Head of Platform
Starlite AI
[Attachment: starlite_sessions.csv (text/csv)]

Thanks for the note and for attaching the sample CSV. We're sorry for the confusion here — I'll triage this with Billing Ops.

I'm looping in Marissa and Jordan from billing to pull the raw metering events and do a first-pass dedupe analysis. We'll get you an initial export and a proposed remediation/credit by EOD Monday.

- Karthik

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Vasquez <elena@starlite.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Feb 2026 14:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Overlapping session counts in Feb 1-3 usage — possible double-counting

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the examples and the patience. We pulled the raw metering events for STL-9001 (Feb 1-3) and ran a dedup analysis. Summary:

- Root cause: For a subset of requests routed through a multi-tenant proxy, the proxy sometimes dropped the session_uuid header on websocket reconnects. Our metering pipeline deduplicates only when session_uuid is present and canonical — when header is missing a reconnect is treated as a new session.
- Impact: ~16.9% of billed tokens during Feb 1-3 appear to be duplicate counts from rapid reconnects (mostly under 10s apart).
- Proposed immediate remediation: We will issue a credit of $1,240.50 against the Feb invoice (line-item: duplicate reconnects). We will also adjust the invoice to reflect the corrected token totals and send an updated invoice PDF.

I've attached an excerpt of the processed usage (redwood_usage_excerpt.ndjson) showing matched pairs and the internal correlation keys we used.

Next steps we're taking:
1) Engineering has a short patch to treat reconnects with matching client_socket_id + proxied IP as candidates for dedup unless explicitly overridden; patch will be deployed to prod Canary tonight.
2) We'll backfill the dedupe for Feb 1-3 (and run a sanity check on surrounding days) and include the backfilled adjustment in the updated invoice.
3) I'll create a support ticket and flag this as P2 for expedited handling: RED-9876.

If you want us to hold the credit until you've verified the updated invoice, let us know — otherwise we'll apply the credit automatically and email the revised invoice.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Billing Ops Lead
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_usage_excerpt.ndjson (application/x-ndjson)]
